1. Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp price spikes — reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% for periods following spikes.

2. Model underestimates true outcomes in the second half of the forecast (e.g., days 15–30), particularly when true values show mean reversion or sharp declines — increase forecast mid-range by 3–7% to account for lagged market correction.

3. Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices in the first 5–7 days of forecast — apply downward adjustment of 1–3% for early forecast days if historical mean is below 35.

4. When true outcomes show sudden drops (e.g., 34.33 or 33.10), model fails to anticipate — add a 5–10% buffer for sharp downward moves in the 3–5 day window following such events.

5. Model tends to overcorrect after high peaks — if forecast peaks exceed true peak by >10%, reduce subsequent forecast values by 5–8% to avoid overshoot.

6. Model underestimates true mean in the final 10 days — adjust forecast mean by +2–5% for the last 10 days if true mean is >40, to reflect market stabilization.
